task_spec:
> Using the Global Weather Repository CSV, produce:
> 1. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest cities**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 2. Two ranked bar charts of the **top 10 hottest countries**, one by average and one by single hottest measurement temperature (celsius)
> 3. **Print the top 10 lists to the console** before plotting: for each of the 4 charts, print the ranked names and their temperature values (e.g., "1. Paris: 25.2 deg C")
> 4. A **100-word summary** for a non-technical audience explaining the rankings and any notable patterns
>
> Column reference: cities are in `location_name`, countries in `country`, temperature in `temperature_celsius`.

report_draft: The world's hottest cities and countries cluster primarily in the Middle East and North Africa, where consistent heat prevails. Ar Riyadh and Kuwait lead by average temperature at 45.0°C and 44.4°C respectively, followed by a gradual drop through tropical regions like Cambodia and Bangladesh. However, the single hottest temperature ever recorded in this dataset tells a different story: Suva, Fiji reached a remarkable 79.3°C—far exceeding any other location. Kuwait City and Baghdad follow with more typical extreme peaks around 49°C. At the country level, Saudi Arabia and Morocco consistently rank highest by average, while Fiji Islands records the extreme outlier. This contrast between average and peak temperatures reveals an important distinction: Middle Eastern cities are persistently hot year-round, while Fiji's extreme reading suggests occasional spikes rather than sustained heat.

report_history.content: The world's hottest cities and countries cluster primarily in the Middle East and North Africa, where consistent heat prevails. Ar Riyadh and Kuwait lead by average temperature, both exceeding 44°C, followed by a gradual drop through tropical regions like Cambodia and Bangladesh. However, the single hottest temperature ever recorded in this dataset tells a different story: Suva, Fiji reached a remarkable 79.3°C—far exceeding any other location. Kuwait City and Baghdad follow with more typical extreme peaks around 49°C. At the country level, Saudi Arabia and Morocco consistently rank highest by average, while Fiji Islands records the extreme outlier. This contrast between average and peak temperatures reveals an important distinction: Middle Eastern cities are persistently hot year-round, while Fiji's extreme reading suggests occasional spikes rather than sustained heat. The data underscores how geography shapes temperature patterns—deserts show steady heat, while tropical island climates can produce rare, intense extremes.
